name: Exorcism
description: A religious or spiritual practice for evicting demons, jinn, or other malevolent entities from a person, place, or object; recognized in Christianity, Judaism, Islam, Hinduism, and Buddhism, with the Catholic 'Roman Ritual' (1614, revised 1999) being the best-known formal rite.
full_description: Exorcism is the religious or spiritual practice of evicting demons, jinn, or other unwanted spiritual entities from a person, place, or object. The English word derives from the Ancient Greek 'exorkismós' ('binding by oath'). Christian exorcism is rooted in New Testament accounts of Jesus casting out demons in the synoptic Gospels and forms part of multiple traditions: in the Catholic Church the formal rite of major exorcism is contained in the 'Rituale Romanum' (the Roman Ritual, instituted 1614 and revised in 1999) and may only be performed by a duly-ordained priest with the bishop's permission, after psychological and medical evaluation; minor exorcisms are part of baptism and other liturgies; the Eastern Orthodox Church trains all priests in exorcism; Lutheran and other Protestant churches retain various forms. Islam practices ruqyah (Quranic-recitation cleansing). Judaism preserves a Kabbalistic rite involving Psalm 91 and the shofar. Hinduism employs mantras, yajnas, and protective texts such as the Hanuman Chalisa. Tibetan Buddhism observes the 'Gutor' rite on the 29th lunar day. Mainstream psychiatric medicine does not recognize demonic possession as a diagnosis; phenomena traditionally interpreted as possession are typically associated with conditions such as schizophrenia, dissociative identity disorder, and temporal-lobe epilepsy. Notable historical cases include Martha Brossier (1578), the 1949 case that inspired William Peter Blatty's 1971 novel 'The Exorcist', and Anneliese Michel (1975–1976), whose death after 67 Catholic exorcisms led to a manslaughter conviction of two priests.

aliases.name: exorkismós
aliases.meaning: 'binding by oath'; etymological root of the modern term

aliases.name: Major exorcism
aliases.meaning: Catholic formal rite according to the Roman Ritual

aliases.name: Minor exorcism
aliases.meaning: Lesser exorcisms in Catholic baptismal and other liturgies

aliases.name: Deliverance ministry
aliases.meaning: Charismatic and Pentecostal practice analogous to exorcism

origin: Exorcism is practiced globally, in every major religious tradition, with regional and confessional variations.

etymology.origin: Latin 'exorcismus', from Ancient Greek 'exorkismós' (ἐξορκισμός) 'a binding by oath', from 'exorkízein' 'to bind by an oath, adjure'.
etymology.meaning: Literally 'binding by oath'; in religious usage, the act of compelling a demon or other spirit to depart by sacred command.
etymology.first_use: Greek and Latin Christian writings of late antiquity; the practice itself is documented in the New Testament (1st century CE) and earlier.

timeline.event: New Testament accounts of Jesus performing exorcisms (synoptic Gospels)
timeline.source: New Testament; Wikipedia: Exorcism in Christianity

timeline.event: Pope Paul V promulgates the 'Rituale Romanum', codifying Catholic exorcism for the Latin Church
timeline.significance: First fully codified Latin-rite exorcism rite

timeline.event: The 'Roland Doe' / 'Robbie Mannheim' case in Cottage City, Maryland and St. Louis, Missouri, in which Catholic priests perform an exorcism
timeline.significance: Inspired William Peter Blatty's 1971 novel 'The Exorcist'

timeline.event: William Peter Blatty publishes 'The Exorcist', adapted as William Friedkin's 1973 film
timeline.significance: Drives the 20th-century cultural revival of interest in exorcism

timeline.event: First exorcism session for Anneliese Michel performed by Father Arnold Renz, with permission from Bishop Josef Stangl of Würzburg
timeline.significance: Beginning of the most-cited modern exorcism case

timeline.event: Anneliese Michel dies of malnutrition and dehydration after 67 exorcism sessions
timeline.significance: Leads to a manslaughter conviction of her parents and the priests Renz and Alt

timeline.event: The Vatican publishes the revised rite of exorcism ('De exorcismis et supplicationibus quibusdam'), the first revision since 1614
timeline.significance: Modernizes the Catholic rite and emphasizes psychiatric collaboration
timeline.source: Wikipedia: Exorcism in the Catholic Church

related.name: Demonic possession
related.description: The condition that exorcism is intended to remedy.

related.name: Shamanic soul retrieval
related.description: Cross-cultural ritual practice of retrieving lost spirits / removing harmful ones.

cultural_notes: Across the major religions, exorcism is held to be both a real spiritual intervention and a serious matter that requires authorized ritual specialists.
